posts.title: Teaching the Art of the Steady Hand: Inside Our Care Practice Room
posts.excerpt: At Mimamori College, foundational caregiving begins with unhurried physical practice, close supervision, and the quiet discipline of listening.
posts.content:
When an adult decides to enter care work, their initial anxiety is almost never about paperwork or classroom theory. It is about physical touch. How do you support someone who is frail without hurting them or straining your own back? How do you assist a person twice your size to stand from a wheelchair without making them feel vulnerable? At Mimamori College, founded in 2009 at 18 Orchard Row in Lindmere, we believe these skills cannot be learned from a textbook or an online video. They are taught through physical practice, one steady hand at a time.

Our training day begins promptly at 08:45. In the classroom, students review resident handover notes, learning to interpret subtle clinical observations before touching a single piece of equipment. But by 09:15, the entire cohort transitions into our practice room. Here, the learning environment is calm, spacious, and deliberate. Four adjustable profiling beds, mobile hoists, and transfer aids stand ready, but what truly defines the room is our staffing ratio: exactly one instructor to eight students. Under this level of supervision, no trainee ever rehearses a transfer in isolation or develops unsafe physical habits.

Lead Instructor Rosa Delgado spends hours teaching trainees how to position their feet, brace their core, and communicate with clarity before initiating any movement. You watch an instructor place a guiding hand gently along a student's forearm, demonstrating how minimal, well-directed force creates stability. Trainees take turns acting as both caregiver and resident. Experiencing what it feels like to be lowered in a hoist sling or turned with slide sheets builds an instinctive empathy that no lecture can instill. When you know firsthand how it feels to have your balance entrusted to someone else, you handle another human being with permanent reverence.

In the afternoons at 13:15, after midday classroom lectures on safeguarding and infection control, our practice room welcomes older community volunteers from the Lindmere area. These sessions allow trainees to navigate the natural rhythms of conversation and daily routines. When an older volunteer sits across from a nineteen-year-old student or a former warehouse supervisor starting over at fifty-two, the barrier of clinical uncertainty dissolves. Director of Practice Samuel Adeyemi and Learner Support lead Daniel Brandt observe each interaction, providing immediate feedback during our daily 15:00 review before the day concludes at 15:30.

This careful preparation explains why our clinical placement model is structured so deliberately across thirty-two weeks. In the Core Care Certificate, students spend Weeks 1 through 8 strictly on campus. No resident is moved by a student who has not been signed off in the practice room. When placements begin in Week 9, students attend two days each week alongside a named mentor at one of our twenty-two partner care homes, such as Larchfield House, Mill Lane Care Home, or The Orchards. Over the course of the program, every learner completes 420 placement hours, culminating in four continuous weeks on the floor alongside their mentor.

The word mimamori means watching over. It describes a protective, attentive presence that respects personal dignity while ensuring safety. In residential care, watching over someone requires patience, keen observation, and physical confidence. Whether you are eighteen years old or changing careers at fifty-two, that confidence is built through repetition, honest feedback, and steady guidance. As our January intake approaches with 14 places remaining, our Lindmere practice room remains dedicated to this enduring craft: preparing caregivers whose hands are steady, capable, and kind.

posts.title: Open morning confirmed for Saturday 21 November at 10:00.
posts.excerpt: Come and see the practice room, the equipment and the instructors. Free, and no need to book.
posts.content:
Our next open morning is on Saturday 21 November at 10:00 at 18 Orchard Row, Lindmere. Come and see the practice room, look at the profiling beds and hoists, and speak with the instructors who teach there. Principal Ingrid Halvorsen and Lead Instructor Rosa Delgado will be on hand to explain the 32-week curriculum and answer questions about placement.

Attendance is free and there is no need to book. If you cannot come on the day, write to hello@mimamoricollege.example and we will arrange a visit on a weekday between 08:30 and 17:30.

posts.title: Evening Route admissions for 12 January.
posts.excerpt: The Evening Route teaches the same certificate over 48 weeks, for people who keep a day job.
posts.content:
Applications are being accepted for the 48-week Evening Route starting on 12 January. It covers the same curriculum as the daytime certificate, on Monday and Wednesday evenings and Saturday practical workshops, and includes the full 420 placement hours.

Tuition is $7,200, payable in four interest-free instalments, with a $180 kit fee. Call +1 555 0142 for the detailed timetable.

posts.title: Bursary applications for new applicants.
posts.excerpt: Up to six bursaries of $1,500 are available for the 12 January intake.
posts.content:
Up to six bursaries of $1,500 each are available for the 12 January intake. They are for applicants who show financial need, and they come off the tuition for the Core Care Certificate or the Evening Route.

To apply, first complete your practical assessment day and hold an offer of admission. Send the bursary form and supporting papers to Daniel Brandt in Learner Support at least four weeks before term begins.

posts.title: Applications open for the 12 January Core Care Certificate cohort.
posts.excerpt: Applications are open for the 12 January Core Care Certificate, with 14 places left in a cohort of 24.
posts.content:
Applications are now open for the full-time Core Care Certificate starting on 12 January. Each intake is limited to 24 students, so that the practice room keeps its ratio of one instructor to eight students, and 14 places remain.

Start with the application form, then book a practical visit and interview. Bursary applications must reach us four weeks before the start date. Questions can go to hello@mimamoricollege.example or +1 555 0142.

posts.title: Practice room safety inductions complete for autumn learners.
posts.excerpt: Every autumn learner has been signed off on brakes, slide sheets and hoists before moving anyone.
posts.content:
All autumn learners have completed their safety induction in the practice room. Before anyone is moved, each student shows that they can check the brakes on a bed and a wheelchair, use slide sheets and a transfer belt, and operate the ceiling hoist with an instructor beside them.

The inductions were led by Director of Practice Samuel Adeyemi. As on every course, no resident is moved by a student who has not been signed off in the practice room.
